title: BUILD_PLAN
description: Structured build plan produced by the planning phase before any code is generated

planning_notes.description: Bounded to three categories only: (a) decisions made against something, with the reason; (b) invariants binding more than one part; (c) the assembly procedure and non-printed hardware it consumes. Not a restatement of any structured field (placement, load, dimensions, etc). Describes the CURRENT design state only -- never a round-by-round changelog; that history belongs exclusively in request_log.

intent_ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC `ts` of the newest request_log entry that `intent` has been reconciled against. Records acknowledgement, not edit: advanced on every clarification/correction, including one that leaves `intent` unchanged. Optional; required by plan_validate.py only when the request_log holds a clarification/correction entry (see the approved-intent spec).

acceptance_ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC `ts` of the newest request_log entry that acceptance.json (the oracle's statements) has been reconciled against. Same acknowledgement rule as intent_ts; required by plan validation only when acceptance.json exists and the request_log holds a clarification/correction entry (see the oracle-acceptance spec).

acceptance_bindings.description: Planner's binding of every acceptance.json statement to plan entities. One entry per (statement, part); `part` is "*" only for a visual statement about the whole model. Checked by oracle.py against the statement (counts, sizes, spacing, extents, probe labels).

probes.description: probes[].label values on that part; a probe statement's label starts with its id

intent.description: The user-approved reformulation written at the Phase 1 exit checkpoint (see the approved-intent spec). States what is being built and why, the confirmed reading of any shape the request left ambiguous, the fit type of every mating surface, every assumption Phase 1 made rather than asked about (each with its concrete value), and the repo-relative sketches/ path of every user-supplied image the design is based on. Does not restate values a structured field already carries in full (dimension table -> parameters.py / parts[].dimensions; printer/material/nozzle -> the plan's own fields). Phase 2 copies this text verbatim and does not author it. minLength 120: excludes a bare noun phrase (shortest eval-corpus reformulation is a two-clause sentence) while a genuinely simple one-part request still passes.

coordinate_frame.description: Resolved compass-to-axis binding for this project's prose and review interpretation only (does not alter placement.rotate or joint dof.direction sign conventions). Defaults to the standard binding (east: +x, north: +y, up: +z, per prompts/planning.md's Coordinate vocabulary table) when absent.

material.description: Default filament material; a part or union may override it

optimize_for.description: Plan-level print-orientation objective. 'strength' (default when omitted) keeps the part's load in the layer plane; 'min_support' minimizes support material; 'visual_quality' favors clean visible surfaces (penalizes gentle inclines under 45 deg, orients the cosmetic show_face against the bed). A per-part optimize_for overrides this for that part.

review_policy.description: Plan-level review-frequency preference for the Phase 3 part loop. 'every_stage' (default when omitted) builds every part progressively with a stage checkpoint and shows the Step 0 profile-stub checkpoint. 'checkpoints' shows the stub checkpoint and applies the existing interfaces/blocks_needed complexity gate to decide progressive vs. autonomous per part. 'minimal' self-reviews the stub without pausing and builds every part autonomously with no stage checkpoints.

parts.description: Ordered list of parts to generate

id.description: Unique snake_case identifier, used as script filename

interfaces.description: Physical connection points with external objects

type.description: Interface category (port_cutout, screw_mount, pcb_mount, snap_fit, etc.)

name.description: The agreed vocabulary word for this feature (same normalized snake_case form as a part id), used for feature labels and legends

connector.description: Connector or standard name for this interface, e.g. usb_c

wall.description: Face the interface sits on (descriptive, e.g. north/south/top)

clearance_mm.description: Per-mate fit clearance for this interface, in mm

position_mm.description: Feature center in the part's build pose [x, y, z] in mm; enables the deterministic feature-presence check

diameter_mm.description: Round-feature diameter in mm (feature-presence size target)

size_mm.description: Rectangular-feature [w, h] in mm (feature-presence size target)

instance.description: blocks_needed instance id this interface positions; a step script's part.positions(id) returns these position_mm values in order

probes.description: Authored intent checks in the part's build pose (same frame as interfaces[].position_mm), seeded into a step script's probe registry as plan-owned probes. Use for request dimensions no positioned, sized interface covers; bracket a wall or step height with a solid_at/empty_at pair. Keep points at least 0.1 mm off any surface.

label.description: The request or plan fact this probe checks

instance.description: blocks_needed instance id whose place step arms this probe; omit to check only at the final check

blocks_needed.description: Blocks from inventory.json required for this part. Each item is either a block name string, or an object carrying the block name plus its instance extents (enables the script-level thin-block DFM check before any code is generated).

extents_mm.description: Block instance bounding box [x, y, z] in mm

id.description: Instance handle, unique within the part; a step script's select(name, id=...) binds to it

params.description: Parameter name -> value for this instance, matching the inventory entry's params; a step script's resize() binds exactly these

edges.description: Cosmetic edge treatment: inventory edge-set name -> size in mm, applied in the print-pose finishing pass (chamfer or fillet per edge direction)

part_notes.description: LLM reasoning for this part: blocks chosen, geometry written from scratch, unusual decisions. Describes the CURRENT design state only -- never a round-by-round changelog; that history belongs exclusively in request_log.

archetype.description: Name of a matching entry in templates/archetypes.json, set by the planner when this part fits an archetype's `use` description. Cross-checked against the archetype index by plan_validate.py. Optional; omit when no archetype fits -- the part loop's own Step 1.5 match still runs either way.

plate.description: Print-group id. Parts sharing a plate print in one job (print-in-place). Defaults to the part's own id (one part per plate) when omitted.

material.description: Filament material for this part's unions; overrides the plan-level `material`. A union's own `material` overrides this. Different materials are treated as non-sticky: nothing relies on adhesion across their boundary.

color.description: Display and filament color (#RRGGBB) for this part's unions; defaults to a color derived from the resolved material.

copy_of.description: Declares this part a copy of another part: no script is authored for it; export reuses the source part's geometry (reflected across the plane normal to `mirror` when given), then applies this part's own placement. The source must be a single-union part and not itself a copy. Use for identical or pairwise-mirrored parts.

mirror.description: Reflect across the plane normal to this axis (through the authored origin) before placement; omit for an identical copy

unions.description: Optional named unions this part's script produces. When present, the script's top-level `result` MUST be a dict mapping each union id to its CadQuery Workplane. When absent, the part is a single union whose id is the part id and whose plate is the part's `plate` (the default). The part's `placement` applies to every union it produces; union ids are unique across the model and are the namespace that `kinematics.moving_union` and plate grouping reference.

id.description: Unique snake_case union id; the per-union STL/object name and the kinematics/plate reference key

plate.description: Print-group id for this union; defaults to the part's `plate`, else the union's `object`, else the union id

material.description: Filament material for this union; defaults to the part's `material`, else the plan's

color.description: Display and filament color (#RRGGBB) for this union; defaults to the part's `color`, else a color derived from the resolved material

object.description: Slicer-object group id. Unions sharing it (at least two, all from this part and on one plate) are exported as the bodies of one slicer object, e.g. the color regions of a multi-color part. Members touch but must not overlap.

filament.description: 1-based filament slot (slicer extruder number) this union prints with. Not checked against the printer; the slicer flags a slot it does not have.

sacrificial.description: True for a union that is designed-in breakaway support (e.g. blocks.breakaway_fin geometry). The quality gate skips it for overhang, sliver, thin-region and brim findings and reports it as `designed_support`. Default false.

load.description: Principal load direction (and type) in the part's own build pose, determined by the planner (rule 10). Drives print-orientation strength scoring: for tension/bending/shear, orientations that keep this direction in the layer plane (perpendicular to build Z) score stronger; for compression, strength is orientation-neutral since a resting load doesn't stress the interlayer bond. Omitting the whole `load` object makes strength orientation-neutral (the optimizer does NOT guess a load axis from geometry) -- only correct when the part truly carries no structural load.

dir.description: Direction vector [x, y, z] in the build pose; need not be unit length

type.description: Load type. tension/bending/shear keep layer-plane strength scoring (default, conservative). compression (a resting weight pressing straight through the part's thickness -- a base, plinth, pedestal, foot) makes strength orientation-neutral so support/bed-contact decide instead.

magnitude_n.description: Load magnitude in newtons, for the FEM stress advisor (src/fem_check.py). Derived from a researched mass (magnitude_n = mass_g * 9.81 / 1000 * safety_factor, see reference/Engineering Design Rules.md) -- never a value the planner invented. Omit when no mass was researched for this part; the advisor then does not run.

applied_at.description: Name of the interfaces[] entry (see interfaces[].name) where this load enters the part, for the FEM stress advisor. Requires the named interface to carry position_mm.

applied_dir.description: Direction override for the applied traction at `applied_at`, for a load entering its interface at an angle to the part's principal `dir` (e.g. a shelf lip that also pushes outward). Affects only the FEM advisor's applied traction; `dir` remains the direction print-orientation scoring and the engineering-rationale trigger read. Omit to apply the load along `dir`.

grounded_at.description: Names of interfaces[] entries that hold the part fixed, for the FEM stress advisor. Each named interface must carry position_mm. Grounds are fully fixed (no direction).

engineering_rationale.description: The part's load reasoning: the single home of the ENGINEERING RATIONALE the part author derives while writing the script, written back into BUILD_PLAN.json after the script is accepted (not authored at plan time). A load-bearing part (declared `load`, or a load-bearing block/archetype -- see the trigger set in plan_validate.py) takes the object form; every other part takes the string form.

oneOf.description: One-line form for a part with no load-bearing features, e.g. 'no load-bearing features (static cosmetic part)'.

load_path.description: Where the load enters the part and how it travels through it.

worst_case_stress.description: The specific location that sees the highest stress.

check.description: A formula evaluated with the script's own parameter names (not free-standing constants), compared against a stated material allowable, e.g. 'strain = 1.5*t*d/L^2 = 1.0% <= 4.0% allowable (PETG)'.

optimize_for.description: Per-part print-orientation objective; overrides the plan-level optimize_for for this part. Omit to inherit the plan-level value (or 'strength' when that is also absent).

show_face.description: Optional outward normal of the part's primary cosmetic surface in its own build pose. Used by the 'visual_quality' optimization mode as the surface to orient face-down against the smooth bed. Omit to let the optimizer infer a cosmetic surface from geometry.

dir.description: Direction vector [x, y, z] in the build pose; need not be unit length

placement.description: Pose of this union in the shared assembly pose. Rotations apply in listed order, then the translation. Omit for identity (union authored directly in the assembly pose). Supplied by the part author during the build phase, as a write-back into BUILD_PLAN.json after the part is accepted -- a value present before then (e.g. from a prior plan) is a proposal for the author to confirm or correct, not an error. A part reached via a `joints` mate chain (see `joints`) MUST NOT declare its own placement -- its pose is derived.

pose_intent.description: The part's goal pose in the shared assembly pose, stated in human-readable terms the author can check against a render (which way it faces, where it sits). Never a restatement of a rotation sequence or translation vector -- that structured form is `placement`, which the part author supplies during the build phase.

kinematics.description: Declared range-of-motion checks for articulating joints, nested into a tree via `children`. Each entry sweeps its moving union (plus everything nested under its `children`) through its required range against every union outside that subtree. Optional; absent or empty skips the kinematic stage.

request_log.description: Append-only verbatim request history: the initial request plus every clarification/correction that shaped the plan. The exclusive place for round-by-round build history -- planning_notes and part_notes describe only the current design state. Optional; absent plans (including eval-corpus goldens) stay valid. When present, exactly one `initial` entry, first in the array (enforced by plan_validate.py, not expressible cleanly in draft-7). `level` and `targets` are optional and independent -- entries written before typed request_log carry neither and stay valid; carried-forward entries are never back-filled. Its pair is `intent_ts`, the reconciliation stamp for `intent`.

images.description: Repo-relative paths to sketch/annotated-image files (copied into sketches/) that motivated this entry

level.description: Intent granularity (LLM4CAD-Editor): functional = adds/removes/reshapes a part or capability; operation = changes how an existing feature is made (a joint, a cut, a pattern); parameter = a dimension/literal change with the design otherwise fixed

targets.description: Affected part ids and/or `part.feature` / parameter names this entry names

script_baseline.description: part id -> SHA-256 of that part's script when this entry was appended (`log.py request add --snapshot-scripts`); quality_gate diffs it to flag a parameter-level correction that leaked into an untargeted part

root_part.description: The one part anchored directly into the world: its own `placement` (identity when absent) is its edge into the assembly pose. Required when `joints` is non-empty; every other part named in a `joints` entry gets its pose derived along the mate chain (BFS spanning tree) from this part instead of declaring its own `placement`.

joints.description: Cross-part matched-pair joints. Each entry names a matched-pair block (one whose inventory descriptor carries `emits`) and its two members, each fusing into a named part. A mated part's assembled pose is derived by composing the mate chain from `root_part`, instead of that part declaring its own `placement`. Cycles are allowed only when every joint on the loop is rigid (its block has no `dof`) and the docks close; a loop through a `dof` joint is rejected. Optional; absent or empty needs no `root_part` and leaves every part's placement mechanism unchanged.

block.description: Matched-pair block name from inventory.json (must carry `emits`)

params.description: Kwargs passed to the block's function call -- the single declared source for this pair's parameters

members.description: The block's two members, each fusing into a part. The two entries must reference the block's two distinct `emits` ids and two distinct parts.

member.description: One of the block's declared `emits` ids

part.description: Id of the part whose script fuses this member in

union.description: Id of the union of `part` this member fuses into. Optional when the part has a single union; required when it declares more than one.

dock.description: This member's pose WITHIN its host part's own build pose (not the assembly pose). Omit for identity.

bom.description: Bill of non-printed materials: hardware the user must supply (screws, nuts, washers, heat-set inserts, magnets, bearings, springs, filament/rod pins, adhesives). Optional; absent plans validate unchanged.

qty.description: Total quantity across the listed parts

parts.description: Part ids that consume this item

wall_min_mm.description: Minimum wall thickness for DFM check

interface_min_area_mm2.description: Minimum area of the join between a placed block and the body it is unioned onto; absent means 4.0

overhang_max_deg.description: Maximum overhang angle before support required

fin_hints.description: Whether the quality gate suggests designed-in breakaway fins (a `fin_hint` info finding) for overhangs it flags. Default true; set false to opt out (e.g. the user wants slicer supports or no support geometry).

bridge_max_mm.description: Longest span (mm), supported on two or more sides, printed as a bridge without support (default 10)

block.description: Joint block name from inventory.json (must carry a dof). Omit for a block-less (directly-declared) joint built from raw primitives; axis_origin_mm/axis_dir/type/required_range/step fully specify the motion in that case.

mechanical_limit.description: Nominal range bound [lo, hi] for a block-less entry, same shape as a block's dof.mechanical_limit. Meaningful only when block is absent; ignored when block is present, since the block's dof remains authoritative.

axis_origin_mm.description: Assembly-pose pivot point [x, y, z] in mm

required_range.description: Range [lo, hi] the design requires, RELATIVE to the union's authored pose (zero), in the field unit. May be negative and may straddle zero (e.g. [-30, 90]).

lo_inclusive.description: Whether the lower bound must be cleared (closed). False = open: lo need not be reached and a collision exactly at lo is not reported.

hi_inclusive.description: Whether the upper bound must be cleared (closed). False = open.

step.description: Sweep increment in the derived unit (deg for revolute/spherical, mm for prismatic)

stop_on_contact.description: True when the joint's travel ends by resting against another body (a folding leaf closing onto its plate) rather than at a specific value. First real interference is then reported as the mechanical stop -- a contact_limited_stop warning naming how far it got -- instead of a motion_collision error, since the mechanism never reaches the interpenetrating poses beyond that stop. Default false: interference inside required_range is an error.

children.description: Nested kinematics entries mounted on this entry's moving_union, recursively forming the joint tree. Omitted/empty means nothing else is mounted on this joint. An entry not listed in any other entry's children is itself mounted on the static frame.

translate_mm.description: Translation [x, y, z] in mm, applied after rotations

rotate.description: Ordered rotation steps about axes through the origin
